text.en: Two children have one paratha and want to share it fairly. If one gets a big piece and the other a small piece, it is not fair. They fold it into two pieces that match exactly, and each gets one half. Then four friends come, and the paratha is cut into four equal parts, called quarters.

A whole thing can be shared equally between two people. Each share is called a half, and two halves make one whole. For a share to be a half, the two parts must be exactly equal. If one part is bigger, it is not a half. We can fold a rectangular sheet in half in more than one way: along the middle from top to bottom, from side to side, or along a diagonal. All the ways give two matching parts. When part of a chikki has been eaten, look at what is left. It may be less than half, exactly half or more than half of the whole piece. We say one half. We do not say one out of two.
Amit shared a mango tree, a lamp and a blanket with his brother by taking the fruit, the night and the winter for himself. That was not fair even though it sounded equal. Sharing is fair when each person gets the same amount of what is useful. We can share things in different fair ways. Mangoes can be shared half and half. The tree can be shared by taking turns each year or by sharing its fruit equally.
Half and double are partners. 3 is half of 6, and 6 is double of 3. 4 marbles are half of 8 marbles, and 8 marbles are double of 4 marbles. To find half of a number we share it equally into two. To find double we add the number to itself. Half of 14 is 7 and double of 7 is 14. On a number line we can see how far a number is from the half or the double. 5 is 2 less than 7, which is half of 14, and 13 is 1 less than 14, which is double of 7.
When a whole is shared equally among four people, each share is called a quarter. Four quarters make one whole. Two quarters together make a half, because the whole is cut in two halves and each half is cut again into two quarters. Three quarters is a whole with one quarter taken away. We say one quarter, two quarters, three quarters and four quarters. A quarter of 16 flowers is 4, and half of 16 flowers is 8. Half is double a quarter, because 8 is double of 4. We can make quarters by folding a paper twice, and the folds can be in different directions as long as the four parts match exactly.
Shabnam and Mukta share a chocolate and a paratha at lunch, and one says, it is not fair, you gave me a bigger part. To check whether two parts are equal, we fold one part over the other and see if the edges match. Shabnam folds the paratha over itself so that both sides fit exactly on each other. Only a paratha that has been cut into two equal parts is shared fairly.
When one whole is shared equally between 2 people, each share is called a half. Two halves make one whole, and we can check this with paper halves. Half of a shape is coloured when the coloured part and the white part are exactly equal. If Shabnam has eaten a chikki from 3 sides, less than half is left, because eating from 3 sides takes away more than half. We can make a half in many ways, such as by folding a rectangle lengthwise, across, or along a diagonal.
The old man gave his sons Amit and Bala a mango tree, a solar lamp and a woollen blanket to share. Amit's plan was not fair, because he kept the fruits, the night time and the winter, which are the best parts. A fair way is to give the tree to one son and the lamp to the other, or to share the fruits equally and take turns with the others. Fair sharing means that both people are happy with the parts they get.
If I have 3 marbles and you have 6, then 3 is half of 6, and 6 is double of 3. 4 marbles are half of 8 marbles, and 8 marbles are double of 4 marbles. 10 marbles are double of 5 marbles, and 5 marbles are half of 10 marbles. Half of 14 is 7, and 5 is 2 less than 7, while double of 7 is 14, and 13 is 1 less than 14, so we can say how far a number is from the half or the double on a number line.
When one whole is divided into 4 equal parts, each part is called a quarter. Half of a half is a quarter, so two quarters make a half. One quarter, two quarters, three quarters and four quarters show how the whole fills up, and four quarters make the complete whole. If 16 flowers are shared, a quarter is 4 flowers and a half is 8 flowers, so the half is double the quarter.

problem.en: A paratha is cut into two pieces. One is bigger. Are these halves?

text.en: Halves must be exactly equal parts.

why.en: The idea of half is equal sharing.

text.en: One piece is bigger.

why.en: So the parts are not equal.

text.en: No, they are not halves.

why.en: To get halves we must cut into two matching parts.

problem.en: Lakshanya has 16 flowers and ties a quarter of them. How many does she tie?

text.en: A quarter means share into 4 equal parts.

why.en: Divide the 16 flowers into 4 equal groups.

text.en: She ties 4 flowers.

problem.en: Half of Peehu's 16 flowers are tied. How many tied flowers is that, and how does it compare with a quarter?

text.en: Half of 16 is 16 ÷ 2 = 8.
A quarter of 16 is 4.
8 is double of 4.

why.en: So half is double a quarter.

problem.en: Ravi has 14 marbles. Mona has half as many. How many does Mona have?

text.en: Half means two equal parts, so share 14 into 2 equal groups.

why.en: Half is sharing equally between two.

text.en: 7 and 7 make 14.

why.en: Check by adding the two parts.

text.en: Mona has 7 marbles.

prompt.en: Explain what a half and a quarter are and how they are related.

requiredIdeas.en: A half is one of two equal parts
A quarter is one of four equal parts

commonMisconceptions.en: Any two pieces can be called halves
A quarter is bigger than a half

points.en: A half is one of two equal parts, and 2 halves make 1 whole.
A quarter is one of four equal parts, and 4 quarters make 1 whole.
2 quarters are the same as a half.
Half and double are partners, 3 is half of 6.
Half of a number is one of two equal shares, and double is twice the number.
Parts are equal only if they match exactly when folded.
Four equal parts are quarters, and four quarters make one whole.
